title: Beneficiary Grievances and Allowable Charge Reviews: Scope and Effect
content:
**Beneficiary Grievance and Allowable Charge Review — scope note, Appeals and Grievances**

*Beneficiary Grievance.* A Beneficiary Grievance is answered in writing within the tier's decision time limit and is referred to clinical quality management where the tier makes a quality referral; it changes no claim, authorization or enrollment and has no next level.

*Allowable Charge Review.* An Allowable Charge Review checks only that the allowed amount was figured under the correct TRICARE maximum allowable charge, prevailing rate or negotiated rate for the service, date and locality; an overturned review reprocesses the line at the corrected allowed amount and the result is final.

*Common limit.* Neither may be used to contest medical necessity or coverage, which have their own tiers.

| | Beneficiary Grievance | Allowable Charge Review |
|---|---|---|
| What is examined | the service, access or conduct complained of | whether the allowed amount was figured under the correct maximum allowable charge, prevailing rate or negotiated rate for the service, date and locality |
| Effect of a favorable outcome | a written answer; no claim, authorization or enrollment changes | the line is reprocessed at the corrected allowed amount |
| Next level | none | none — the result is final |
| Medical necessity or coverage | not contestable here | not contestable here |
